correctness.rationale: The 12 truncated tetrahedron vertices V_ij=2A_i+A_j have norm²=11, exactly 18 edge pairs with squared distance 8, and no three vertex rays coplanar. Twelve normal great circles with pairwise transverse intersections give 134 cells. Exhaustive integer sign enumeration of 528 local crossing-quadrant witnesses produces all 134 unique sign masks, classifies six chamber types and their spherical-angle coefficient vectors. The resulting P4,P5,P6 sum to one and E N=18 acos(7/11)/π, independently from common edge angle. Independent implementation reconstructed all six class multiplicities and probabilities.
residual_risks: Exact integer finite classification proves all possible normal cells because each lies adjacent to a great-circle intersection; floating approximations not used for sign masks.
The claim addresses only generic central planar sections of the precisely normalized regular truncated tetrahedron.

originality.rationale: A natural complete Haar central-section polygon-count law for the regular truncated tetrahedron: three possible planar section vertex counts, six spherical chamber classes and their exact angle-sum areas. Prior published general polytope section-vertex attainable-count and combinatorial directional function results do not imply the six area values or probability vector for this Archimedean solid.
